text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- President Martti Ahtisaari has appealed to Russian prime minister Viktor Tshernomyrdin for a quick solution to the cargo truck dispute between the two countries.
- National meditor Jorma Reini suspended from office pending police investigations on allegations of violent behaviour before and during police arrest.
- A parliamentary committee on EU affairs evaluating Finland's activities in the EU says ministers and officials are more interested in compromise than to promote Finland's interests.
- Clinic treating drug-abuse planned to start 24-hour service in Helsinki in 1998.
- Subsidised housing construction would not be an economically feasible way to boost economic growth, says head of the Government Institute of Economic Research (VATT).
- Investor Pentti Kouri, infamous for his involvement in Unitas' and KOP's corner operations in each other in 1988-89, plans comeback on the Finnish financial scene.
- The tender rate could still be lowered from 3.00 percent which is the same as the German repo rate, says the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA).
- Three companies set joint venture Internet advertising agency Netbooking Oy.
- Finland should not introduce legislation to approve euthanasia, says archdeacon Risto Pelkonen.
